  • Method Details

    • guiEyesAdvanceWithoutWorldTicks

      public static void guiEyesAdvanceWithoutWorldTicks(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Inventory icons keep their own clock, so their expressions continue while the world is paused. In game: in single player with ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:blink"] and ambientMinTicks = 1 and ambientMaxTicks = 1 in somegoogly-server.toml, open your inventory with a Googly Eye in it and press Esc to pause; the icon keeps blinking while mobs behind the menu stand still.

    • guiEyesHonorEligibilityAndSwitch

      public static void guiEyesHonorEligibilityAndSwitch(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Only eye items get animated icons, and hiding eyes discards icon state, so showing them again starts fresh. In game: put a Googly Eye, a plain skull, and a diamond in your inventory; only the eye's pupil moves. Set disableGooglyEyes = true in somegoogly-client.toml; the icon is drawn plain. Set it back; the pupil moves again, starting from rest.

    • guiEyesKeepPresentationIdentity

      public static void guiEyesKeepPresentationIdentity(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A slot keeps its eye's simulation when the stack is copied or its count changes, and the pupil falls toward screen-down. In game: with a stack of Googly Eyes in a slot, right-click to pick up half and put it back; the slot's pupil keeps moving smoothly instead of jumping back to rest.

    • guiEyesReplaceChangedContents

      public static void guiEyesReplaceChangedContents(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A changed appearance gives a slot's eye a new simulation with the new look. In game: put a Googly Eye in a slot, then replace it with a dyed or glowing one; the icon shows the new color or glow at once.

    • guiEyesRetireClosedAndHiddenViews

      public static void guiEyesRetireClosedAndHiddenViews(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Closing a screen frees its icons' state, the hotbar's icons keep theirs, and icons out of view expire. No visible in-game form, since a fresh pupil starts at rest where the old one settled; guards that closed chests, changed screens, and creative entries scrolled out of view leave no state behind.

    • guiEyesSeparateSlotsAndCursor

      public static void guiEyesSeparateSlotsAndCursor(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Each slot and the carried stack animate on their own. In game: fill several slots with Googly Eyes and pick up another stack with the cursor; the slots blink at different times, and the carried eye keeps its own pupil and expressions as you drag it across the occupied slots.

    • guiHeadUsesConfiguredLayout

      public static void guiHeadUsesConfiguredLayout(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      An eyed head in the inventory shows its mob's eyes in place, and both eyes can blink and cross, independent of the same head in a frame. In game: with ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:blink", "somegoogly:cross_eye"] in somegoogly-server.toml, put eyed skeleton skulls in your inventory and a chest and frame another; the icons show both eyes at normal icon size, blink and cross, and do so at different times from the framed skull.

    • nestedDrawContextsRestoreOuterSelection

      public static void nestedDrawContextsRestoreOuterSelection(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      One nested draw context carries GUI identity, the selected animation, and the item being drawn; closing an inner scope restores the enclosing one. A GUI item's animation is selected inside its slot's scope while its render state is filled, and the state carries that selection to its later draw, which no GUI scope encloses. In game: put eyed heads and Googly Eyes in inventory slots, the hotbar, and item frames; each animates on its own and a head drawn inside another item's slot keeps its eyes.
